chapters.title: Ticket configuration
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It explains how to shape the tickets everyone works with.
You set the statuses and their transitions, the categories and issue types, and the extra fields. You also design ticket forms and set numbering and lifecycle rules.

sections.title: Ticket configuration at a glance
intro: Changes apply to the next request. Open desks refresh by themselves.

rows: The statuses agents move tickets through, and which moves are allowed.
Two levels of categories, and the nature of each request.
Extra fields for tickets, contacts and customers.
How fields are arranged on the agent and portal ticket forms.
The ticket number prefix, reopen and auto-close rules, merge and split, surveys, and priority labels.

blocks.tip: The **Fields & form layouts** card on the **Administration** home opens **Custom fields** directly.

sections.title: Statuses
intro: Every status belongs to one fixed category: **Open**, **Assigned**, **In progress**, **Waiting**, **Resolved** or **Closed**. Reports, SLAs and the portal rely on the categories.
Built-in statuses have a lock badge. You can rename them, but you cannot delete them.

blocks.caption: The **Statuses** section with eight statuses in display order.
blocks.alt: Statuses list with numbered section tabs, New status button, drag handle, status badges, ticket count, order arrows and Edit button

callouts: The ticket configuration sections.
**New status**.
The drag handle. Drag a row to change the display order.
The status name with badges for category, **Default**, **Pauses SLA**, **Inactive** and **Built-in**. The line below shows the allowed next statuses, the customer label and substatuses.
How many tickets have the status now.
The arrows also move the status up or down.
**Edit** opens the status.

blocks.note: A new order is saved as soon as you drag a row or select an arrow.

sections.title: Create or edit a status
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Statuses**.

steps.text: Select **New status**, or **Edit** on a status.
steps.caption: The **Edit status** panel for Waiting on Customer.
steps.alt: Edit status panel with name, category, colour, customer label, switches, allowed next statuses and substatuses

steps: Enter the **Name**, and choose the **Category** and **Colour**.
Enter a **Label shown to customers** to keep the internal name private in the portal.
Turn on **Default status of its category** or **Pause SLA resolution clocks while in this status** if needed.
Under **Allowed next statuses**, leave **Any status (no restriction)** on, or turn it off and tick the allowed statuses.
In **Substatuses**, type a finer reason and press [[Enter]]. Repeat for each one.
Select **Create status** or **Save status**.
sections.result: A message says "Status created" or "Status saved". The list shows the new settings.

rows: Fixed for built-in statuses and for statuses in use.
A colour code such as `#d97706`, or pick one.
**Pause SLA resolution clocks while in this status**
Stops the next response and resolution clocks.
With restrictions on, tick at least one status.
Built-in statuses cannot be turned off.

blocks.note: Every category must keep at least one active status. Tickets that follow a blueprint ignore the allowed next statuses. The blueprint decides.

sections.title: Delete a status
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Statuses** and select **Edit** on the status.
Select **Delete**.
In the confirmation, select **Delete**.
sections.result: A message says "Status deleted". Transitions that pointed to it are removed too.

blocks.tip: If tickets still use the status, turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Categories and issue types
intro: Categories classify what a ticket is about. They have two levels: a category and its subcategories. A category can be limited to one department.
Issue types describe the nature of the request, such as a question, an incident or a change request.

blocks.caption: The **Categories & issue types** section.
blocks.alt: Categories and issue types with numbered Category button, a category row, Sub button, a subcategory, Issue type button and issue type list

callouts: **Category** adds a top-level category.
A category with its department badge and ticket count.
**Sub** adds a subcategory to that category.
A subcategory. **Agents only** marks items hidden from the portal.
**Issue type** adds an issue type.
The issue types with their ticket counts.

blocks.p: Use the arrows on a row to change the order. The new order is saved at once.
Priorities and severities have fixed values. You can change only their labels and colours. See [Change numbering and lifecycle settings](#ticket-settings-task).

sections.title: Add or edit a category
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Categories & issue types**.

steps.text: Select **Category**, or **Sub** on a category. To edit, select the category's name.
steps.caption: The **New category** panel.
steps.alt: New category panel with name, parent category, department and two switches

steps: Enter the **Name**.
Choose a **Parent category**, or keep **None — top-level category**.
Choose a **Department**, or keep **All departments**.
Turn **Customers can choose it in the portal** on or off.
Select **Save**.

blocks.note: To delete a category, open it and select **Delete**. Delete or move its subcategories first. A category that tickets use cannot be deleted. Turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Add or edit an issue type
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Categories & issue types**.
Select **Issue type**, or select the name of an issue type.
Enter the **Name** and a **Description**.
Select **Save**.

blocks.note: An issue type that tickets use cannot be deleted. Turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Custom fields
sections.intro: Custom fields capture information your process needs, such as an ERP module or a vendor reference. They exist for tickets, contacts and customers.

blocks.caption: The **Custom fields** section with six ticket fields.
blocks.alt: Custom fields list with numbered record type tabs, New field button, field name and badges, order arrows and Edit button

callouts: Tabs for **Ticket fields**, **Contact fields** and **Customer fields**.
**New field**.
The field label, key and type, with badges such as **Required** and **Portal: editable**.
The arrows change the order of the fields.
**Edit** opens the field.

blocks.p: The line under each field shows its departments, the layouts that use it and its help text.

sections.title: Create a custom field
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Custom fields**.

steps.caption: A new picklist field with two options.
steps.alt: New field panel with record type, type, label, key, options, default value, help text, visibility and required settings

steps: Choose the **Record type** and the **Type**.
Enter the **Label**. The **Key** fills in by itself, and you can change it before you save.
For a picklist, add the **Options**. For a record lookup, choose what it **Looks up**.
Optionally, enter a **Default value**, **Help text** and validation limits.
Under **Visibility** and **Required**, turn on the settings you need.
For a ticket field, optionally choose **Departments**.
Select **Create field**.
sections.result: A message says "Field created". Agents see the field on the matching records.

blocks.warning: You cannot change the **Key** or the **Type** after you create the field.

rows: 2–63 lower-case letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter. Unique for the record type.
1–500 options, each with a value and a label.
For text fields only. The length can be 1–10000.
Shows the field in the customer portal.
**Customers can fill it in when raising a ticket**
Needs the field to be visible in the portal.
**Always required when the record is created or edited**
Agents must fill it in every time.
Ticket fields only. The field must be filled in before a ticket may enter those statuses.
Ticket fields only. Leave empty to use the field everywhere.

blocks.note: Agents always see every active field.

rows: A longer text over several lines.
One value from a list of options.
Several values from a list of options.
A link to a web page.
A link to a product, customer, contact, user or installation.

sections.title: Delete a custom field
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Custom fields** and select **Edit** on the field.
Select **Delete**.
In the confirmation, type the field's key.
Select **Delete field**.
sections.result: A message says "Field deleted". The field disappears from every form layout.

blocks.note: Values already stored on records are kept, but they are no longer shown. To hide a field for now, turn off **Active** instead.

sections.title: Form layouts
intro: A form layout arranges ticket fields in sections and columns. It is either an **Agent ticket form** or a **Portal (customer) form**.
Without a layout, forms show every field that applies, in the default order.

blocks.caption: The **Form layouts** section before any layout exists.
blocks.alt: Form layouts section with an explanation, the New layout button and an empty state with Design a form

list: The most specific active layout wins. A layout for the ticket's department, and its brand or channel, comes first.
Otherwise, the default layout of the form applies.
Only one active layout can cover the same form, department, brand and channel.

blocks.p: Portal forms take only fields customers may fill in. These are department, priority, category, product, installation and custom fields set as editable in the portal. Layouts are for tickets only.

sections.title: Design a form layout
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Form layouts** and select **New layout**.
Enter a **Name** and choose the **Form**.
Choose a **Department**, and a **Brand** for portal forms or a **Channel** for agent forms.
Turn on **Default agent form** or **Default portal form** if this is the default.
Select **Add section**. Give it a title and choose 1, 2 or 3 columns.
Drag fields from **Available fields** into a section, or select the plus button on a field.
Tick **Required** on fields that agents or customers must fill in.
Select **Preview** to check the form, then **Design** to go back.
Select **Create layout**.
sections.result: A message says "Layout created". The layout appears under **Agent forms** or **Portal forms**.

blocks.caption: The layout builder for a new agent form.
blocks.alt: Layout builder with numbered settings card, Design and Preview tabs, Available fields, a section header, a Required box, Add section and the save bar

callouts: The layout settings: name, form, department, channel or brand, **Default** and **Active**.
**Design** and **Preview**.
**Available fields**. **custom** marks custom fields. **Filter fields** finds one.
A section: title, number of columns, order arrows and the delete button.
**Required**. **Subject** and **Department** are always required.
**Add section**. A layout can have up to 20 sections.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Create layout** or **Save layout**.

blocks.caption: The **Preview** of the new agent form. Controls are inactive.
blocks.alt: Form preview with the Request and Classification sections

sections.title: Edit or delete a form layout
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Form layouts**.
To change a layout, select **Edit** on it, make your changes, then select **Save layout**.
To remove a layout, select its delete button, then **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: A saved layout applies to the next form that opens. After a delete, forms fall back to the next matching layout.

sections.title: Numbering and lifecycle
sections.intro: The **Numbering & lifecycle** section holds workspace-wide ticket rules on one page.

blocks.caption: The **Numbering & lifecycle** section.
blocks.alt: Numbering and lifecycle page with numbered cards for numbering, lifecycle, merge and split, surveys, priorities and severities, and the save bar

callouts: **Ticket numbering**: the prefix and a sample of the next number.
**Lifecycle**: reopening, automatic closure and resolution rules.
**Merge & split**: limits for merging duplicates and splitting messages.
**Satisfaction surveys**: the survey sent when a ticket is resolved.
**Priorities & severities**: labels and colours of the fixed values.
The save bar with **Discard** and **Save settings**.

rows: Shown before every ticket number, such as `#`, `SD-` or `WS/`.
Numbers have no gaps within your workspace.
A customer reply inside the window reopens the ticket. A later reply creates a follow-up ticket.
Resolved tickets close by themselves after this time. 0 means never.
How long an agent's edit lock lasts without activity.
**Customers may reopen resolved tickets (within the window)**
Lets customers reopen from the portal.
Agents must use the confirm option when they resolve.
Agents must pick a resolution code.
**Acknowledge new e-mail tickets automatically (where the mailbox allows it)**
Sends an automatic reply to new e-mail tickets.
The most tickets one merge can combine.
**Allow splitting messages into a new ticket**
Agents can move a message into a new ticket.
**Send a survey when a ticket is resolved**
How long the survey link works.

blocks.note: Resolution codes, root causes and close reasons have no screen yet. To change them, import them with **Configuration transfer**.

sections.title: Change numbering and lifecycle settings
steps: Open **Ticket configuration** > **Numbering & lifecycle**.
Change the **Prefix**, the day and minute limits, and the switches you need.
Under **Priorities & severities**, change a label or pick a new colour. The pill beside it shows the result.
Select **Save settings**.
sections.result: A message says "Ticket settings saved". The save bar shows the new version number.

blocks.warning: A new prefix changes how every ticket number is shown, including old tickets. Tell your team before you change it.

troubleshooting.problem: "Every category needs at least one active status."
troubleshooting.cause: You turned off the last active status of a category.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep at least one active status in each category, or create another one first.
Rename it, or turn off **Active** if the category has another active status.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says tickets use the status you want to delete.
troubleshooting.fix: Move those tickets to another status, or turn off **Active**.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says tickets use the category or issue type you want to delete.
troubleshooting.cause: Tickets refer to the category or issue type.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn off **Active**. The item disappears from forms but stays on old tickets.
Delete the subcategories, or give them another parent category.

troubleshooting.cause: Keys must be unique for each record type.

troubleshooting.problem: "A field must be visible in the portal to be editable there."
troubleshooting.cause: **Customers can fill it in when raising a ticket** is on, but **Customers see it in the portal** is off.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on **Customers see it in the portal** too.

troubleshooting.problem: "Another active layout already covers this department, brand and channel."
troubleshooting.cause: Two active layouts would apply to the same form.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the department, brand or channel, or turn off **Active** on one layout.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says a field cannot be placed on a portal form.
troubleshooting.cause: The field is not one customers may fill in.
troubleshooting.fix: Use it on an agent form, or set the custom field as editable in the portal.

faq.q: Can I rename the built-in statuses?
faq.a: Yes. You can rename them and change their colour and customer label. You cannot delete them or change their category.

faq.q: Why can a ticket not move to a status I expect?
faq.a: The current status may restrict the allowed next statuses. Tickets that follow a blueprint use the blueprint's moves instead.

faq.q: What happens to stored values when I delete a custom field?
faq.a: They are kept but hidden. The field is removed from every form layout.

faq.q: Do I need a form layout?
faq.a: No. Without a layout, forms show every field that applies in the default order. Layouts let you group, order and require fields.

glossary.definition: An extra field that an administrator adds to tickets, contacts or customers.
An arrangement of ticket fields in sections and columns for the agent form or the portal form.
The nature of a request, such as a question, an incident or a change request.
The number of days after resolution during which a customer reply reopens a ticket.
One of six fixed groups that every status belongs to: Open, Assigned, In progress, Waiting, Resolved or Closed.
A finer reason within a status, such as Vendor within Waiting on Third Party.
